summary: W. F. Jayasuriya was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. D. Rouse was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Regent's Park College and Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Headmaster of The Perse School (1902–1928) and Sanskrit Lecturer at Christ's College, Cambridge (1903–1939).

W. H. R. Rivers studied medicine at St Bartholomew's and the University of London. He was Lecturer in Psychology at Cambridge (1893–1908), Fellow of St John's College, and served as President of the Royal Anthropological Institute (1921–1922).

W. Haskell was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Dartmouth and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught Greek and Latin at East Maine Conference Seminary and served as a librarian at Yale University (1875–1905).

W. Norman Brown earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton. An Indology and history scholar, he became Professor of Sanskrit at Johns Hopkins and long-time Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1926–1966).

W. Randolph Kloetzli, active in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (1964) under scholars including Frank E. Reynolds and J. A. B. van Buitenen. He taught at American University, George Washington, and Dartmouth.

W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

W. W. Tarn was a historian and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eton College and Trinity College, Cambridge, where he later served as a Fellow from approximately 1938 to 1957.

Wadigala Samitharathana specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed an MA at SOAS (2023–2024) and an MPhil at Oxford (2024), and became Founding President and Managing Trustee of the Oxford Buddhist Society in 2023.

Wai-lun Tam earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. Working in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, he served as professor and Chairperson of Cultural and Religious Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walenty Skorochód Majewski was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collegium Nobilium, where he became a teacher in 1785. In 1808, he took charge of the Central Archives of Historical Records.

Walpola Rahula studied at Vidyalankara Pirivena, Ceylon, Calcutta, and Paris under G. P. Malalasekera and Paul Demiéville. A Buddhist studies scholar, he was Professor at Northwestern (1964) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964–1969).

Walter A. Fairservis, Jr. studied at Chicago, Columbia, and Harvard. An archaeologist and Indologist, he was Director of the Burke Museum (1962–1968), Curator at the American Museum of Natural History (1968–1976), and Professor of Anthropology at Vassar College (1968).

Walter Anthony Cook was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Woodstock College, De Nobili College, St. Mary's College, and Georgetown University, where he served as Professor of Linguistics from approximately 1966 to 1993.

Walter Bruno Henning earned his PhD at Göttingen under Friedrich Carl Andreas. A specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, he taught at SOAS (1936–1961) and served as Professor of Iranian Studies at UC Berkeley (1961–1967).

Walter Clawiter was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt in approximately 1958 and held a post there from about 1958 to 1970.

Walter Couvreur studied at KU Leuven under Albert Joseph Carnoy and at Göttingen under Emil Sieg. A linguist and Indologist, he held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research and Ghent University, becoming Professor of IE Linguistics in 1949.
Walter Denecke was an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1923. He studied under Hermann Jacobi and Walther Schubring.

Walter Elliot was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology who studied at East India Company College and the College of Fort St. George. He served the Government of Madras and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Madras (1859–1860).

Walter Emile van Wijk, an Indologist and historian, studied at Leiden University, later serving as privatdozent of chronology there. He also was Director of Museon (1933–1938) and Director of the Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris (1938–1953).
